title: C-O7b: `orchestrator handover` — write the restart checkpoint into plan.md from bus state so a Planner can resume on another account with one command
spec:
Why: when the Planner session dies at a subscription limit, the next session on the other account resumes from .orchestrator/plan.md and the bus; today the checkpoint is only as fresh as the Planner's last manual write. Implement orchestrator/handover.py write(reason: str) -> Path: under the bus lock, replace (or append when absent) a section `## Auto-handover <ISO timestamp, Europe/Zurich> — <reason>` at the end of plan.md containing: open goals (parentless triage tasks not done) with title; per goal the child tasks grouped by status (queued with depends_on, running with executor and started time, held with hold_reason and resume_hint keys, done-not-merged, merged with sha); the worktrees that exist under wt/; the last 5 events from bus.events; and the sentence "Resume: skill resume; re-spawn held spec reviews; dispatch ready execute tasks by hand while Codex cools." Keep the section under 120 lines by truncating lists with "… and N more". cli.py: `handover [--reason TEXT]` (default reason "manual"). Idempotent: a second call replaces the section, it never duplicates it, and the rest of plan.md is byte-identical. Also: daemon.tick() calls handover.write("daemon tick") at most once every 15 minutes (a timestamp in pool_state), so the checkpoint is never older than that even when the Planner is gone. Tests in tests/test_handover.py with the harness fixtures: section content per status group, truncation, idempotent replace preserving the rest of the file, daemon throttle (two ticks within 15 min write once). README.md: two lines under Run it.
(Recreated from T-0108: re-pointed at the recreated C-O7a)
acceptance: tests/test_handover.py: writes_section_with_status_groups, truncates_long_lists, replaces_section_idempotently_and_preserves_rest, daemon_throttles_to_15_min; all green
`uv run orchestrator handover --reason test` appends exactly one Auto-handover section to .orchestrator/plan.md in a scratch root and a second run leaves one section
`uv run python -m unittest discover -q tests` green; no new dependency

result.summary:
Committed on `task/T-0119`.

## Summary
Implemented `orchestrator/handover.py` with `write(reason) -> Path`: under the bus lock it replaces (or appends) a `## Auto-handover <ISO Europe/Zurich timestamp> — <reason>` section at the end of `plan.md`, listing open goals (parentless `triage` tasks not done), each goal's child tasks grouped by status (queued/depends_on, running/executor+started, held/hold_reason+resume_hint keys, done-not-merged, merged/sha), worktrees under `wt/`, the last 5 bus events, and the fixed "Resume: ..." sentence — with per-list and section-wide truncation to stay under 120 lines while always preserving the resume sentence. `cli.py` gained `handover [--reason TEXT]` (default `manual`). `daemon.py` gained `maybe_handover()`, called from `tick()`, throttled to once per 15 minutes via a `handover_last_at` timestamp merged directly into `pool_state.json` (not through `Pool.save()`, which only knows its own fields and would drop the key). README got two lines under "Run it".

**Files changed:** `orchestrator/handover.py` (new), `orchestrator/daemon.py`, `orchestrator/cli.py`, `tests/test_handover.py` (new), `README.md`.

**Test output:** `uv run python -m unittest discover -q tests` → 211 tests, all green (only pre-existing sqlite `ResourceWarning` noise, unrelated). `.claude/hooks/tests-green.sh` (the actual gate script; `scripts/tests_green.sh` doesn't exist in this repo) exits 0. Manual CLI check in a scratch `ORCH_ROOT` confirmed a second `orchestrator handover` call leaves exactly one `## Auto-handover` heading.
result.review: other account, different model; label PR same-family-review
